Command SQL: what the SQL of a command flow may bind, call and touch. The paragraphs below cover actor bindings, parameter bindings, the SQL function list, tables, generated values and app triggers; declaring the command itself is in `connector_commands`.

Actor bindings: command SQL may bind `${{ user.id }}`, `${{ user.group_id }}`, `${{ user.role }}` (the actor's global `_benmore_users.role`, never a tenant membership role) and `${{ user.is_admin }}` (1 for a global framework admin, else 0; a connector actor gets the value but no admin bypass) in the SQL bindings of any phase (prepare, apply, readback), and `${{ user.email }}` in apply SQL only (elsewhere review refuses `trusted actor email must be the exact apply SQL binding`). They come from the live actor re-resolved for that phase, are sealed into the operation at prepare (a role or admin change before approve/commit refuses it), are never taken from client input, are not allowed in set/compute/respond/if or dependency params, and deactivated or password-change-required accounts never reach a binding.

Parameter bindings: a command SQL binding (`:name` bound to `${{ params.x }}`) may name any declared string, integer, number or boolean property, including an optional or nullable one. A missing or null value binds SQL NULL, so write the SQL with COALESCE(:x, ...) instead of making callers pass an empty string; a boolean binds 1 or 0 and a number binds as an integer when whole, else a finite float. An omitted optional param referenced by the prepare respond is sealed in the prepared arguments as an explicit null when its prepared_schema field is nullable, and left out of the sealed arguments when it is not (so an optional, non-nullable argument can really be omitted); either way the SQL binds NULL and the approved operation is one deterministic shape. for_each sources (the array and its elements alike), dependency params and transfer paths require a required, non-nullable path, and `| default:` is not supported in command bindings.

SQL functions: command SQL may call only abs, avg, char, coalesce, concat, concat_ws, count, date, datetime, benmore_today, glob, hex, ifnull, instr, length, like, lower, ltrim, max, min, nullif, printf, quote, replace, round, rtrim, sign, sqlite_version, substr, substring, sum, time, total, trim, typeof, unicode, upper, zeroblob, julianday, strftime and json, json_array, json_array_length, json_group_array, json_extract, json_insert, json_object, json_patch, json_remove, json_replace, json_set, json_type, json_valid, json_quote, under the table-enrollment, scope, transaction and result-size guards. Command SQL runs with SQLite's length limit at 4 MiB: no string, blob or row it reads, builds or writes may be larger. Review, `mcp check`/`inspect`, the push write gate and `benmore check` refuse any other call (random, randomblob, iif) in a dependency query or phase SQL, naming the tool, statement and function; they compile each statement as `dependency_shape` describes. At run time such a call fails with the final code invalid_declaration. For an unguessable value use `generated:` below.

Tables: command SQL cannot name an undeclared table or write framework tables. Apply SQL may insert into, delete from or re-key a table that other tables reference: SQLite's foreign-key enforcement then reads each referencing table's key column, and exactly those columns are admitted while an apply write runs, without adding them to the command's declared reads or digests.

Generated values: a command that needs an unguessable value (an invitation token) declares `command.generated: [{name: invite_token, kind: token, bytes: 24}]` (1..16 entries, bytes 16..64, optional encoding base64url or hex) instead of calling random()/randomblob(). Prepare draws each value once from a cryptographic random source and seals it into the prepared arguments as arguments.generated.<name> (a fixed-length string added to prepared_schema; neither prepared_schema nor the input schema may declare a property named generated), so approval, commit, a retried attempt and a replay all see the same value and every operation draws its own. Apply and readback bind it as ${{ params.generated.<name> }}; the prepare response may reference it, which is the only way it reaches the preview; prepare SQL cannot bind it; a params.generated reference that does not name one declared value is refused at review, and whole ${{ params }} never includes it. The mcp_command_prepare audit row keeps a digest of each value (generated_digests), never the value.

App triggers: enrollment for approved writes accepts an app-authored trigger on an enrolled table only when a write command declares it: `command.app_triggers: [{table, name}]` points at a CREATE TRIGGER in a reviewed migrations/*.sql UP section. The live sqlite_schema text must match that statement (whitespace, comments and keyword case ignored), and the tables its body writes and the tables its WHEN clause and body select from join the enrolled set (reads and writes recursively). A body that touches a _benmore_* or other non-app table, uses OR REPLACE, runs anything but SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, or calls a function outside the SQL function list above plus raise, current_timestamp, benmore_encrypt, benmore_encrypt_plaintext, benmore_ciphertext_matches and benmore_ciphertext_holds is refused at enrollment, not at first use; undeclared, changed, schema.sql-made or missing triggers fail enrollment (`benmore docs connector`).
